& (a+b)^{-1}(a^{-1}+b^{-1})\\
\equiv~ & (a+b)^{-1}(a^{-1}+b^{-1})(ab)(ab)^{-1}\\
\equiv~ & (a+b)^{-1}(a^{-1}ab+abb^{-1})(ab)^{-1}\\
\equiv~ & (a+b)^{-1}(a+b)(ab)^{-1}\\
\equiv~ & (ab)^{-1}\\
\equiv~ & \boxed{2}\pmod n
\end{align*}

To simplify $a^{-1}+b^{-1}$, we can find a common denominator to add the fractions. The common denominator would be $ab$, so $a^{-1}+b^{-1} = \frac{b+a}{ab}$.

Given that $(ab)^{-1}\equiv 2\pmod n$, we can substitute this into our expression for $a^{-1}+b^{-1}$. This gives us $a^{-1}+b^{-1} \equiv 2(b+a) \pmod n$.
